tldr: This incremental technical note proves the matching absolute point-CATE risk and finite-honest connected-interval length frontier when binary outcomes pass through a known outcome-only randomized-response channel. Covariates remain exactly public uniform and treatment remains observed with unknown rough propensity; the causal contrast is Lipschitz while both arm means may be rough. For every finite sample size and positive channel strength, both criteria have order \(\min\{1,\max\{(n\delta^2)^{-1/3},(n\delta)^{-1/4}\}\}\), with no logarithmic loss, a unique crossover at \(\delta=n^{-1/5}\), and consistency exactly when \(n\delta^2\to\infty\). The proof supplies total original-record procedures, universal constants, all-scale occupancy closure, and the finite-honesty converse. Both the unequal-information architecture and amplitude-sensitive full-likelihood certificate MC18--MC37 belong to the annotation donor; the incremental contribution is their legal shrinking-radius specialization and original-record finite-honesty closure. The destination-specific lower argument preserves the full public-treatment likelihood before attenuating outcome-report factors. Central-DP CATE-function releases and integer annotation use different experiments; the note proves the stated frontier without claiming general experiment equivalence or deficiency bounds.
